content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper proposed a new framework for singe stage pose estimation based on the mixture density model. The proposed framework is named MDPose and models the instance localization and keypoints estimation simultaneously. This paper also proposed a training strategy, Random Keypoint Grouping, to further facilitate the training progress. The experiments on the COCO dataset and the OCHuman dataset show that the proposed method is comparable to some of the previous methods.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
### Strength:
1. The idea of modeling multi-instance keypoints by a mixture density model is interesting and seems novel to me. 
2. The paper is well-written and easy to follow. 

### Weaknesses:
1. The experiments are not comprehensive and some important experiments are missing.
* The proposed method should be compared with some latest methods[1]. There is still a gap in accuracy between the proposed method and the CID method, i.e. 68.9 (CID, HRNet-W32)  vs 65.6 (MDPose).
* The paper argues that the proposed method can increase the capacity for distinguishing multiple occluded people, however, it does not show the results on the CrowdPose Dataset[2]. The experiment result on this dataset is needed to prove the effectiveness of the proposed method.
* The proposed method uses a smaller backbone in the experiments, i.e. ResNet-50 and ResNet 101. The experiment settings make it hard to have a fair comparison with the prior art. It is better to show the proposed method with a similar backbone: HRNet-W32  and HRNet-W48.

2. It is a little hard to understand the result in Table 1. Why does the setting of K_g = 18 not work at all? What is the limitation of the group size? Some experiments should be performed by removing some keypoints from the output of the neural network. For example, you can predict 16 keypoints by removing 2 keypoints from the original label.

3. Why does the proposed method use all the mixture components for each keypoints? How about only considering the adjacent ones? A comparison between the two settings is needed.


[1] Wang. et al. Contextual Instance Decoupling for Robust Multi-Person Pose Estimation, CVPR, 2022

[2]Li. et al., CrowdPose: Efficient Crowded Scenes Pose Estimation and A New Benchmark, CVPR, 2019
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
The submission is well-written and easy to follow. 

The authors have committed to releasing the code, so the proposed method can be reproduced in the future. 

The key idea of using a mixture model for multi-person pose estimation seems novel to me.

In conclusion, I think this paper needs additional study before being published at this time, but I will reconsider the final decision if the author can provide more analysis.

content.summary_of_the_paper: This work proposes MDPose, a one-stage multi-person 2D pose estimation method that uses instance-aware mixture density estimation as an alternative to bottom-up or top-down approaches. It applies prior arts in mixture density object detection and adopts it to the 2D human keypoint detection problem. The main innovation lies in Random Keypoint Grouping (RKG), which alleviates the underflow problem introduced by modeling a large number of keypoints for the human body. Experiment results show that the proposed method achieves state-of-the-art results on multi-person pose estimation, while also achieving SOTA inference speed.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
- The proposed method is intuitive and well-motivated. By using a dense-pixel-wise-mixture model, it removes the need for detection and keypoint association steps. The proposed RKG scheme is a novel approach to applying the mixture models in the human pose estimation problem, as the human body contains way more keypoints than detection tasks.
- Results on various 2D pose estimation benchmarks show that the proposed method is effective in estimating pose in a generic setting and excels at estimating pose in occluded images. The main advantage is at inference time, where the proposed method achieves state-of-the-art.

## Weakness

- The main innovation of the paper is adopting the proposed pipeline MDOD[1] to 2D human pose estimation, and specifically on the RKG part where such an issue is not as severe in object detection. The existence of MDOD does undermine the novelty of this work somewhat, but not significantly.

[1] Yoo, J., Lee, H., Chung, I., Seo, G., & Kwak, N. (2021). Training Multi-Object Detector by Estimating Bounding Box Distribution for Input Image. *2021 IEEE/CVF International Conference on Computer Vision (ICCV)*
, 3417-3426.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: The paper is well-written and clear. The material is presented in a well-flowed way and related works are properly cited. It is an extension of the object detection framework, MDOD, in the 2D human pose estimation task, and proposes Random Keypoint Grouping as the main adaption to the large number of human keypoints. Compared to SOTA multi-person pose estimation problem, the main advantage is runtime while maintaining competitive results. The paper should be relatively easy to reproduce.
content.summary_of_the_review: In all, I find the paper novel and a decent contribution to the multi-person pose estimation literature. Since using mixture-density-based method in pose estimation has not been explored much in, I find it novel. The results seem comprehensive and substantiate the claims made in the paper.

content.summary_of_the_paper:
This work presents "MDPose" a real-time multi-person pose estimation method. It achieves high-speed inference time and competitive results in terms of accuracy w.r.t. previous methods.
This method work as a bottom-up approach to the 2D pose estimation problem: firstly the keypoints are extracted in the image, and then are grouped to identify which keypoint belong to which person.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strenghts: 
--The key of this work is the representation of each person as a component of a mixture density model. As result, keypoints estimation can be achieved without any additional identification process. 

--Also, they present the RKG approach to learn the high-dimensional joint distribution, which enables the possibility of not using heuristics and skipping the grouping phase.



weaknesses: 

. The proposed method has a lot in common with the work from Yoo et al (2021), but applied to 2d pose estimation instead of object detection and using the Laplacian distribution instead of the Cauchy distribution (although comparison and motivation are covered partially in the method section and extensively in the appendix).

- The authors claim they are more robust to occlusions, but little evidence has been provided. More experiments with occluded poses should be reported.


- The overall performances are below the competitors.  Although the results are competitive, this accuracy loss is not negligible.


-

Quality: more experiments are needed to convince about all the claims sold with the paper, in particular the occlusions

Originality: - Removing the necessity of performing the grouping step gives a very big boost in the inference speed, and the approach itself is clever, although the novelty seems limited w.r.t. related works.

novelty:  overlap with Yoo et al (2021)

content.summary_of_the_paper: In this paper, the author presents MDPose to solve the multi-person pose estimation problem. in particular, MDPose is based on mixture density which models the joint distribution as in Laplacian style, and is trained with negative log-likelihood. The proposed method is evaluated on several benchmarks and achieve comparable accuray or superior speed with SOTAs.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength:
1. The paper is well written
2. The method achieves good results.

Weakness:
1. Actually, it is not new to utilize mixture density or model joint distribution from the perspective of statistics, such as RLE model in [A] for 2D pose estimation and DAS model [B] for 3D pose estimation. Both of the above models can be used in the multi-person case. The proposed MDPose explore the same modeling strategy of joint distribution and log-likelihood based method for optimizing. The only increamental work is introducing Random Keypoint Grouping for partitioning joints. However, this RKG module needs a heyper-parameter for pre-setting the person number, which is not flexible in practice. So, the contribution of this paper is very limited

[A] Li et al., Human Pose Regression with Residual Log-likelihood Estimation, in ICCV 2021
[B] Wang et al., Distribution-Aware Single-Stage Models for Multi-Person 3D Pose Estimation, in CVPR 2022
